healthcareSystem: Public healthcare is free but severely under-resourced. Georgetown Public Hospital is the main facility. Private hospitals in Georgetown offer better care. Interior regions have only basic health posts.
qualityNotes: Basic healthcare in Georgetown. Private facilities are better than public ones. English is spoken everywhere. Interior and Rupununi region have extremely limited access. Serious conditions require evacuation to Trinidad, Barbados, or Miami.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Georgetown open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-2pm Saturday. Very limited options in the interior.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Georgetown are reasonably stocked. English is spoken. Bring all medications for interior/Rupununi travel. Counterfeit drugs can be a concern — buy from reputable pharmacies.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is loose. Many medications available OTC. English-speaking country. Bring essential medications from home, especially for interior travel.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. Keep medications in original packaging. English documentation is accepted. Bring generous extra supplies for interior travel.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential, especially for interior/Rupununi travel. Evacuation from the interior requires charter flights. Ensure coverage includes adventure activities and remote area travel.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is required for all travelers. Malaria is present in the interior — antimalarial prophylaxis essential for Rupununi, Kaieteur, and rainforest travel. Dengue present in coastal areas.

waterNotes: Tap water in Georgetown is not reliably safe. Use bottled or boiled water. In the interior, all water must be treated or purified. Hotels in Georgetown generally provide safe drinking water.
foodSafetyTips: Food at established restaurants in Georgetown is generally safe. Guyanese cuisine is diverse (Indian, African, Creole, Amerindian). Be cautious with street food. In the interior, eat only well-cooked food. Pepperpot (national dish) is safe at restaurants.
medicalTourismNote: Guyana is not a medical tourism destination. Patients needing specialist care travel to Trinidad, Barbados, or Miami.
metaDescription: Health guide for Guyana: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation (GPHC)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Largest facility in Guyana. Emergency department. Can be overcrowded. English-speaking.

hospitals.name: St. Joseph Mercy Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private Catholic hospital. Better standard of care than public facilities. English-speaking.

hospitals.name: Woodlands Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital. Modern facility by Guyanese standards. Preferred by expats. English-speaking.

hospitals.name: Balwant Singh Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital. General medicine and surgery. English-speaking staff.

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available in Georgetown. Very limited outside the capital.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Georgetown offer decent care. English-speaking. Equipment varies.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Several private dental clinics in Georgetown accept walk-ins. GPHC has dental services for emergencies.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited but available in Georgetown. English is the official language.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited. Some counselors available through NGOs and private practice in Georgetown.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is very limited. Georgetown streets are uneven with open drainage canals. Interior travel is extremely challenging for mobility-impaired travelers.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals have basic ground-floor access. Purpose-built accessibility features are rare.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Minibuses are cramped. Taxis available. Interior travel requires small aircraft and boats.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Georgetown is challenging due to uneven sidewalks and open canals. Interior destinations (Kaieteur Falls, Rupununi) require strenuous travel. Beach and riverside lodges vary — confirm accessibility in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at GPHC and private labs in Georgetown.
covidStatus.notes: Malaria (interior), dengue (coast), and yellow fever are more significant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront cash payment (Guyanese Dollars or USD). Keep all receipts. English documentation provided. Private hospitals may assist with insurance paperwork.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public healthcare is free but very basic. Local currency is Guyanese Dollar (GYD).

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential, especially for interior travel. Interior evacuations require charter flights to Georgetown first, then onward air ambulance. Trinidad is the closest destination with good hospitals.

drugNameMap.note: Commonwealth brands common. Panadol widely recognized.
